title: Elysian Cloud - Redwood partner discovery
summary: Introductory discovery call between Redwood and Elysian Cloud to explore partnership for offering Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments on Elysian's GPU-enabled regions. Reviewed high level GTM, technical integration touchpoints (VPC peering, private control plane, KMS), potential joint benchmarks, and initial commercial signals. Agreed next steps include sharing partner integration checklist, security/infra docs, and scheduling a follow-up technical deep dive for infra team.
action_items: Ethan Liu -> Share partner one-pager and integration checklist (due 2026-06-03)
Priya Raman -> Draft baseline benchmark plan and sample prompt set (due 2026-06-07)
Ravi Menon -> Provide region/instance SKU and estimated pricing for reserved capacity (due 2026-06-04)
Marco DeLuca -> Introduce Elysian infra lead on follow-up invite (due 2026-06-02)
next_steps: Redwood to send partner deck, security FAQ, and integration checklist
Schedule technical deep dive with Elysian infra (2 weeks)
Run initial benchmark on a small dedicated pool (POC scope)
transcript:
[00:00:03] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan Liu, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood. Um, we also have Priya, our solutions engineer, and Carlos from partnerships. Quick intros?
[00:00:15] Marco (Elysian): Hi, Marco here, head of partnerships at Elysian. Anya and Ravi are with me.
[00:00:22] Anya (Elysian): Hi all. Glad to be here.
[00:00:25] Ravi (Elysian): Hey, yeah thanks.
[00:00:28] Priya (Redwood): Cool, thanks. The objective for today is to do a partner intro and discovery, figure out what a collaboration looks like for Elysian hosting Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments on your GPU regions. We'll cover technical needs and GTM.
[00:00:42] Marco: Sounds good. High level — Elysian runs managed GPU regions in EU and NA, and we're expanding APAC next quarter. We want to partner with inference plat- — inference platforms to offer a turnkey stack for customers.
[00:00:56] Ethan: Great. A few qualifying q's: Who are your target customers for this offering, are they mostly enterprises or ISVs? And what level of isolation are you expecting?
[00:01:10] Marco: Primarily enterprise, some mid-market ISVs. Isolation varies — some want dedicated pools and some want VPC-peered private deployments. So both models are interesting.
[00:01:23] Priya: Okay, good. On Redwood side, we offer three deployment modes: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For a partner like Elysian we'd typically do Dedicated first, then map Private for customers who need VPC and KMS.
[00:01:40] Anya: Can you clarify Private — is the control plane still Redwood-managed or fully customer-managed?
[00:01:46] Priya: It's configurable. We have a private control plane option where the control plane sits in your VPC and communicates with Redwood for management, or we can do a customer-managed control plane with an on-prem style setup if needed. There's a little bit of nuance around KMS and audit logs — we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for keys, and we ship audit logs to your SIEM.
[00:02:06] Ravi: That KMS integration is key for some of our financial customers. Do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSMs?
[00:02:14] Priya: Yes to AWS and GCP KMS, and we have a partner integration story for HSMs — it's not out-of-the-box in all cases but we can do an integration path.
[00:02:22] Carlos (Redwood): On compliance, we have SOC2 Type II, and we can share the security package. We also support SAML SSO and RBAC for team controls.
[00:02:32] Marco: Great. On infra — what about instance SKUs and GPU types? Our platform uses A100 equivalents right now but we also offer H100 and some custom Ampere gen X in certain zones.
[00:02:45] Priya: Redwood runtime supports common accelerator families; performance profiles vary. For H100 we're seeing better latency on very large models and better throughput for batched workloads. We'll need to map your actual SKU names to our kernel selection matrix, and run a small benchmark.
[00:03:05] Ethan: Cost conversation — will customers buy Redwood via Elysian procurement or directly from Redwood? We can support both; partners often surface Redwood as a managed offering with referral or reseller pricing. What is Elysian's preference?
[00:03:18] Marco: Initially we'd sell it as an add-on managed service — Elysian contracts with end customer and we contract with Redwood. We want flexible pricing though — some customers will want direct billing.
[00:03:29] Ethan: That makes sense. We can do referral % or reseller margins; we'll get finance to model this once we see expected scale.
[00:03:36] Anya: For integration patterns — what's the networking model for Dedicated? Do you need VPN or can we do VPC peering, private link, etc?
[00:03:45] Priya: We support VPC peering and private link. For Dedicated we usually provision a reserved pool in your region and connect via VPC peering + NAT. For Private deployments we can sit inside your network more directly.
[00:03:58] Ravi: Latency targets — we typically guarantee tail latency for customers. What latency SLOs can Redwood hit on your Dedicated pools?
[00:04:06] Priya: It depends on model size, batch settings, and KV cache hit rates. For medium seq lengths for a LLaMA 70B variant we can hit p95 in the 150-300ms range on H100 with appropriate batching; smaller models are much lower. We'll produce a model profile and perf matrix for your SKUs.
[00:04:26] Marco: Okay. What about autoscaling and burst capacity? Our customers like seamless autoscaling.
[00:04:32] Priya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. There's also smart routing so requests can fall back to a hosted model variant if Dedicated capacity is exhausted — reduces outage risk.
[00:04:46] Anya: Security review — we'll need SOC2 artifacts, pen test summary, and network diagrams for our procurement.
[00:04:53] Carlos: We'll share our security FAQ and SOC2 report. Also, we can do a joint security session with your team to go over details.
[00:04:59] Ravi: For POC/benchmarks: what sample data do you need? We have some anonymized prompts and evaluation sets.
[00:05:07] Priya: A small prompt set and a few representative traffic patterns is ideal — for example, token distributions, average seq length, and any long-tail cases. We'll also want to know concurrency targets so we size the pool correctly.
[00:05:19] Marco: Timeline — we'd like to announce a partner offering around Q3, so a POC in June would be ideal.
[00:05:26] Ethan: That aligns. Proposed next steps: we'll send the partner one-pager, integration checklist, and security package. Priya will draft a baseline benchmark plan. Can we get the infra lead from Elysian on a technical deep dive in ~2 weeks?
[00:05:42] Marco: Yes, I'll loop in our infra lead and propose times.
[00:05:46] Anya: A few quick clarifying q's — how does billing work for Dedicated if the customer exceeds reserved capacity?
[00:05:53] Priya: There's usually an overage rate; for partners we can model burst credits or priced burst tiers. We'll include sample pricing tables in the partner materials.
[00:06:03] Ravi: One more — telemetry and observability. Do you surface token-level cost and latency breakdowns to customers?
[00:06:09] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, tracing hooks, and error analysis. We can send screenshots.
[00:06:19] Ethan: Okay, any blockers from your side?
[00:06:22] Marco: Security review timeline might be the gating factor, and our procurement has specific contract language around data residency for certain customers.
[00:06:31] Carlos: We can accommodate residency via region pinning and Private deployments; we'll surface contract templates early.
[00:06:38] Anya: Sounds good.
[00:06:40] Priya: Alright I'll note action items: benchmark plan, sample prompts, mapping of SKUs and telemetry.
[00:06:48] Ethan: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and follow up with a technical deep dive invite.
[00:06:54] Marco: Thanks all.
[00:06:56] [END]
notes: References: partner deck link (shared post call), security FAQ (shared), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared). Some transcription artifacts present: 'inference plat' instead of 'inference platform', occasional name misspellings.
